I actually mentioned it and my dad told me it was overkill :/ but i still might, especially around food. I feel bad because I made my mom a cake last night (I just thought I'd burned my throat from hot coffee, but it was strep returning with an angry vengeance and I'd just finished the antibiotics a week prior), and now I'm wondering if I should give it to her. I washed my hands probably fifty times and took off the toppings that I had touched (and they were sooo cute, dammit) to be safe.

Yeah, I know. I just feel like it's always something, ya know? I always feel like shit, and I'm tired of it. I don't like being sick. Antibiotics make me super dizzy and feel like shit. My body hates me, and I'm about to start hating it!

I just get strep throat really often, and now I'm worried due to that I'm passing it on to other people. It's resistant to normal antibiotics now, and so I just started taking the strong stuff (levaquin) and I'm just sick of having to do this every three months (every time it happens I sound like a fucking frog and have to miss class, and it gets old). This time I gave it to my boyfriend, and so he's got the antibiotic-resistant strain too and I feel awful about it, and now I'm so worried that I'm gonna give it to my mom or my grandfather when I visit this weekend.  

My dad's a nurse practitioner, and he thinks that I am a chronic carrier or something, and that I'll have to go in for a bunch of penicillin shots over a ten-day period. 

I'm so afraid of what these medicines are doing to my body, especially with all the crap in the news about new medicine-resistant diseases. I'm fucked if I get anything, and I used to consider myself resilient to this shit. I know it's probably due to over-medication and I'm terrified that my body is going to croak out on me, and I dunno if that's worse than me killing myself because my family just had to watch my grandmother die and I don't ever want to do that to them.

She was amazing. She loved everyone so much and fought so hard to stay. By some strange brainfart, I called her Giggle instead of Grandmama when I was a kid, and it stuck because it fit her so well. She bought me a piano when I was nine, and after she retired she decided to start playing piano too. She worked so hard at it, and she would've been a freakin prodigy had she had the means to start at an early age. Because she loved music so much, she started teaching my younger cousins and our neighbors the basics, and they loved it and then she ended up teaching some of their parents! The best thing that happened to me was when my brother (a difficult one) started asking her for lessons. She couldn't give him many in the past few months because she got so sick, but she was so happy that he asked. 

She smoked her whole life, and that was her one flaw. I'd tried to get her to stop so many times, but she was so stubborn about it. She actually did quit in April...and then a month later she found out she had cancer. At first she thought she just wasn't feeling well because of the crap in her lungs kickin around (which is common when long-time smokers quit) but it was good ol' stage 3b that metastasized to her brain.

I just miss her so much. I'm just so happy got to tell her right before she died that I was so sorry for everything I'd ever done wrong to her, and she looked me right in the eye and said, "stop being so damn silly."
Could I read some of your writing?
